title: BACE: Safety & Workplace Culture - Biotechnology - Situational Safety
subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: You encounter a spill of an unknown liquid in the hallway. What is the **first** action you should take?
options: Immediately mop it up to prevent slipping.
Alert others in the area, isolate the scene, and notify a supervisor.
Smell the liquid to identify it.
Pour bleach on it to neutralize potential pathogens.
questions.explain: The first priority in any unknown spill is safety and containment. You must alert others to keep them away, isolate the area, and notify a supervisor or safety officer who can properly identify the hazard before cleanup begins.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: While working in a BSL-2 lab, you accidentally prick your finger with a needle containing human blood. What is the correct order of operations?
options: Report to supervisor -> Wash wound -> Seek medical attention
Wash wound with soap and water -> Report to supervisor -> Seek medical attention
Squeeze the wound to bleed it out -> Bandage it -> Go home
Sanitize the needle -> Finish the experiment -> Wash hands
questions.explain: Immediate first aid is the priority. 1. Wash the site with soap and water immediately. 2. Notify the supervisor. 3. Seek immediate medical evaluation for potential post-exposure prophylaxis.
questions.subject: Biotechnology

questions.q: During a power outage, the chemical fume hood alarm sounds and flow stops. You are working with a volatile toxic chemical. What should you do?
options: Cap the chemical container, close the sash, and alert others.
Leave the sash open to ventilate the room.
Turn on a fan to blow fumes away.
questions.explain: If ventilation fails, containment is the priority. Cap the container to stop vapor release, close the hood sash to isolate the fumes, and warn others to leave the area.
